newsitem.title: USA: Riscorp to restructure, reduce workforce.
newsitem.headline: Riscorp to restructure, reduce workforce.

text.p: RISCORP Inc said Thursday it will reduce its workforce by 17 percent as part of a reorganization to refocus its operations and reduce expenses.
The company said it plans to refocus its operations around its core managed workers' compensation insurance business.
The company said it stopped writing new business owners' policies as of June 1, for a property casualty line it entered in January 1996.

RISCORP also said it is restructuring its financial operations to better meet its regulatory reporting responsibilities with Departments of Insurance, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and NASDAQ.
As part of its refocusing, the company said it will take measures to reduce overall expenses for the remainder of 1997 and beyond.
In the near term, the company's total annual payroll and payroll expenses will be reduced by about $9.9 million, or nearly 28 percent.
Moving forward, the company will conduct an ongoing evaluation to reduce overall expenses on a continuing basis.
However, RISCORP said it does not currently expect to make any further personnel reductions.

As part of the reorganization, RISCORP said it will consolidate operations into three regional offices: Sarasota, servicing Florida; Birmingham, servicing Alabama; and Charlotte, servicing North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.
Effective July 1997, the company will close its offices in Ft. Lauderdale, Fla.; Montgomery, Ala.; Oklahoma City, Okla.; Kansas City, Kan.; Atlanta; and Richmond.
Some personnel will remain in the Montgomery and Oklahoma City offices beyond July to assist in the orderly transition of operations.

In all, the company said it will eliminate about 141 positions, including 59 employees and management personnel in its Sarasota headquarters. About 26 RISCORP employees whose positions are being eliminated have been offered employment elsewhere within the company.
Prior to these employment reductions, RISCORP Inc employed 516 people in its Sarasota headquarters and 836 people companywide.

The company said it plans to maintain its current business and insurance licenses in Oklahoma, Kansas, Missouri and Virginia until those policies expire but will write no new business in those states.
"These workforce reductions were made looking toward the future," RISCORP chief executive Frederick Dawson.

"Significantly, while approximately 17 percent of the workforce is being reduced, we are reducing total annual payroll and payroll expenses by approximately 28 percent, largely through the elimination of senior and executive management positions," he said.

As part of its restructuring of its financial operations, the company said it is outsourcing its financial reporting function to Buttner Hammock Ranes & Co., P.A., a forensic accounting firm based in Jacksonville, Fla.
RISCORP also said that its auditors and Buttner Hammock continue to work on completing both the statutory and GAAP year-end audits for 1996.

Once these are completed, the company will file its audited statutory statements, its 10-K annual statement for 1996, and its 10-Q for the first quarter of 1997 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
The company provided no specific target date for the filings.
